text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.1% today as oil prices climbed on news that Chinese refiners are restricting fuel exports to protect domestic supplies, which reduces global fuel availability and supports crude demand. Brent crude moved above $100 a barrel, and the report of the export ban helped lift the stock back from a five-day slide that had dragged it down 5% from late September.

The energy sector is caught between competing pressures right now: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and potential U.S. policy shifts (like the threatened diesel export ban) are creating uncertainty, while actual supply constraints—like China's fuel export restrictions and tanker security issues through the Strait of Hormuz—are putting a floor under oil prices. That tension explains why the stock dropped sharply last week but found support today.
